content: The Department of Health Policy and Administration (HPAA) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is one of eight departments within the School of Public Health. It is structured to prepare future executive leaders in public health and health administration. The department offers three levels of curriculum: undergraduate, master’s, and doctorate. Additionally, it provides one-year certificate programs in disaster management and healthcare quality. The master’s program includes online options for the Master of Health Administration (MHA) and Master of Public Health (MPH). The Department of Health Policy and Administration was one of the original four departments established when the School of Public Health at UNC-Chapel Hill was officially founded on June 7, 1940. This made it the first public school of public health in the United States. Initially part of the School of Medicine, the department expanded its faculty in the 1960s to include experts in public administration, sociology, healthcare finance, and healthcare administration, responding to the growing demand for health administrators following the introduction of medical care legislation. In 1969, the department launched the Off-Campus Master’s Program, becoming the first public health program in the country to offer courses off-campus. Programs were initially held in Raleigh, followed by Asheville in 1974 and Fayetteville in 1977. The department offers three levels of degrees: baccalaureate, master’s, and doctorate. It also provides two certificate programs in disaster management and patient safety. These programs are designed to equip future health leaders and professionals with the executive training and knowledge necessary to manage health organizations effectively in the 21st century. The curriculum includes traditional health administration coursework in financial management and health law, as well as core public health courses in epidemiology, environmental health, and health behavior. The Bachelor of Science in Public Health (BSPH) degree is designed for students aiming for careers in various healthcare settings, including inpatient, ambulatory, and primary care facilities, public health organizations, health insurance companies, and government agencies. The program also prepares students for roles in policy analysis and program development in health services research organizations. Graduates of the BSPH program have successfully pursued advanced degrees in fields such as public health, law, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, business administration, and health services research. Students begin coursework in their junior year, with a sequenced program designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of healthcare services organization in the U.S. and skills for effective management of health system resources. An internship experience between the junior and senior years allows students to apply their skills, anticipate learning needs, and clarify career goals. The Residential Master’s Program offers three degrees: Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH), and Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA). The MPH is a professional degree for students with a doctoral-level professional degree or a PhD. The MSPH prepares students for careers in health policy analysis, planning, development, evaluation, and advocacy at various levels, including local, state, federal, and international, as well as in the private sector. The MHA is designed for students pursuing management careers in health systems, hospitals, consulting firms, managed care organizations, insurance firms, medical group practices, government agencies, and other healthcare settings. Unlike the Executive Master’s Program, all courses in the Residential Master’s Program are taught on the UNC-Chapel Hill campus. Students typically take three classes per semester, completing the program in two years. MHA and MSPH students must complete 61 credit hours, while MPH students must complete 42 credit hours. Additionally, MHA and MSPH students must complete a 12-week internship, and MPH students must complete a 6-week internship. The Executive Master’s Program (EMP) is designed for working health professionals who wish to remain employed while pursuing an advanced degree. The program offers online tracks for the MHA and MPH degrees. The MPH degree is tailored for students seeking executive or management careers in public health, while the MHA degree is for those pursuing managerial or executive positions in healthcare. The MHA program takes three years to complete and includes additional courses in financial management, operations, and marketing. The MHA requires 60 credit hours for graduation, while the MPH requires 48. The EMP combines online coursework with three on-campus visits to UNC-Chapel Hill, totaling 24 on-campus days. This hybrid format allows students to benefit from distance learning while engaging in-person with colleagues and faculty. The online MHA and MPH programs admit 40 students per cohort, with two cohorts starting each year in December and August. Admission requirements include a GRE score in the 50th percentile and a minimum of three years of healthcare experience. The average age of Executive students is 35. The Master of Science in Disaster Management (MSDM) program is the newest degree offered by the department. The program is primarily aimed at professionals working in disaster-related fields, such as fire, law enforcement, emergency management, veterinary medicine, allied health, emergency medical services, the military, and public health. Other healthcare officials, such as hospital administrators and government personnel, are also expected to be interested. The program is taught almost entirely online, with the first cohort expected to begin in 2008, enrolling approximately 35 students per year. The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program is designed for students seeking the academic foundation and research experience to become independent researchers and educators. The department offers two collaborative PhD programs, one in pharmacy and another in occupational safety and health. The curriculum includes courses in research design, quantitative methods, health services research, and health policy. Students also develop expertise in a substantive area through their minor. The program is designed to be completed in four years. A collaborative PhD program with the School of Pharmacy’s Division of Pharmaceutical Outcomes and Policy allows students to specialize in pharmacoeconomics and pharmaceutical outcomes research. The Doctoral Program in Health Leadership (DrPH) is the only program of its kind in the country to offer a comprehensive DrPH program via distance learning. It prepares mid-level healthcare professionals to become top leaders. The coursework is delivered almost entirely online, allowing students from across the country to participate while remaining employed. Students visit Chapel Hill for four to five days at the beginning of their studies and between semesters. The third year focuses on dissertation writing, with students allowed to take up to two electives. Each credit hour requires approximately 40 hours of student time, amounting to about 240 hours per semester. This workload is manageable for full-time working professionals. The Community Preparedness and Disaster Management Certificate Program provides community leaders, emergency management personnel, and other disaster responders with the latest knowledge of management systems for natural and man-made disasters, including bioterrorism. The program consists of four online courses completed in one year. Three of the four courses can be transferred into a graduate degree program. Topics include disaster management systems at local, state, and national levels, the implications of various disaster scenarios, forensic epidemiology, risk assessment, and cost/benefit analysis. The Healthcare Quality and Patient Safety Certificate Program is a one-year program designed for professionals working to improve quality and performance in healthcare organizations. It consists of four online courses (12 credit hours), three of which can be transferred into a graduate degree program. Students learn about approaches for collecting and analyzing quality of care data, strategies for measuring quality from various perspectives, evaluation of quality improvement movements, analysis of the business case for quality, and guidance on program development, implementation, and evaluation. Several faculty members in the department have received prestigious awards. For example, three faculty members won the John D. Thompson Prize for Young Investigators from the Association of University Programs in Health Administration. Other notable awards include the Distinguished Service Award from the American Association of Public Health Dentistry, the Mark S. Ehrenreich Prize in Healthcare Ethics, and the Vision Award for groundbreaking research in chronic illness care. Faculty and students have also received recognition from organizations such as the Department of Veterans Affairs, the International Health Economics Association, and the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research. The department is currently ranked 3 among top health administration programs in the U.S. Its Executive Master’s Program is ranked 1 by Modern Healthcare as the top health administration program for physician-executives. The School of Public Health is ranked as the leading public school of public health, tied with Harvard University overall.
